perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; directed reroute: Complete oeq:sharp-release-fiber by incorporating the released outcome distributions, latent within-bin disintegrations, and all-radius mass constraints into sharp side-specific endpoint programs, then prove their attainability within the same class.

verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves matched absolute-risk, squared-risk, and honest-expected-length orders max{n^(-1/4),Delta} on its explicitly constructed unknown-design class, using one same-class lower pair that combines sampling and aliasing. Its population identification result is weaker: the observable interval is only an outer bound, and the exact release-specific endpoints and sharp maximal fiber diameter remain open. The framing generally discloses this distinction and does not falsely call the outer interval sharp, but the claimed partial-identification contribution therefore settles only worst-case diameter order, not the identified set itself. The result is also confined to the specially defined experiment in which angle, raw radius, and raw coordinates are completely suppressed, without an inclusion or transfer theorem connecting that experiment and law class to the published boundary-discontinuity classes, which keeps the contribution below the field floor.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Complete oeq:sharp-release-fiber by incorporating the released outcome distributions, latent within-bin disintegrations, and all-radius mass constraints into sharp side-specific endpoint programs, then prove their attainability within the same class.
